comment: What each Linux build adds on top of the upstream release it is made from.
The key is the full tag without its release- prefix, as in 3.6.6-linux1.
generate-release-notes.ts turns the entries into a section of the release
notes, above the upstream changelog. Leaving a version out of this file is
fine: the section is then left out too.
This file is ours. It sits next to the upstream changelog.json rather than
inside it, so that merging an upstream release never conflicts here.

3.6.7-beta2-linux3: Preview build, made from the upstream 3.6.7 beta 2: it carries what the next release will bring, and the bugs a beta comes with
Also available as a Flatpak, from the beta channel of the package repository or as a .flatpak file: either way, flatpak update brings the betas that follow
The package repository serves the .deb, the .rpm and the Flatpak on its beta channel, and keeps them up to date through apt, dnf or flatpak: <https://packages-github-desktop.nitramo.fr/>
The application itself is the same as in 3.6.7-beta2-linux2
The .deb package is numbered below the 3.6.7 release it precedes, so that apt moves on to that release once it is out
If you installed the .deb of 3.6.7-beta2-linux1, install this one by hand: apt reads its corrected number as older
Beta channel features are enabled, as in the official beta builds
The window shows its own icon under Wayland, and groups with its launcher in the taskbar
Ptyxis is detected as a terminal, along with the editors and shells upstream added since 3.4.13
